search_log: Searched “Nights in Rodanthe Nicholas Sparks excerpt,” “first chapter,” and publisher/author-site variants; found the author-hosted PDF and the permission-reprinted Bookreporter excerpt.

Searched “Nights in Rodanthe third person point of view,” “narrator,” and “alternating point of view”; found an explicit whole-book third-person description, while school blogs and synopsis-only results were treated as weak discovery material.
Searched the official Nicholas Sparks work page and writing notes for frame, letter, diary, and structural evidence; the author confirms quoted letters and describes Adrienne’s storytelling frame.

Ran exact-phrase searches for the apparent first-person quotes; available context located q00270, q00273, q00275, q00277, q00281, and q00283 in letters and q00276, q00278, and q00279 in character dialogue. Unofficial full-text snippets were used only to locate context, not as primary person evidence.
No credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person base sections or alternating narrative person was found.
person_note: The controlling prose is third person, with sustained external narration of Adrienne and Paul. The strongest quote evidence is q00288 and q00289, corroborated by the authorized opening excerpt and the explicit whole-book description. The numerous first-person quotations are local material—principally Paul’s letters and dialogue by Adrienne—and therefore do not create a first-person strand or an alternating structure. Several clipped or isolated third-person-looking quotes remain locally nondiagnostic, but that uncertainty does not affect the well-supported book-level classification.
